summary:
INFINIX: HUMAN SURVIVAL EXPERIMENT ON MARS is a browser-based Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer designed for children aged 7–12. Players take on the role of astronauts responsible for sustaining their team's lives throughout a 30-day mission on Mars.

Players manage five essential mission systems: life support, radiation shielding, food production, power management and communication delays. They make decisions involving limited resources and trade-offs while responding to unexpected emergencies.

Through interactive gameplay, INFINIX introduces children to the challenges and responsibilities of space exploration while developing their critical thinking, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
details:
INFINIX is a browser-based Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer designed for children aged 7–12. Players manage a Martian crew for 30 days by controlling five systems: life support, radiation shielding, food production, power management and communication delays. They must manage resources, make decisions and respond to emergencies to ensure survival.

The game makes space science fun and easier to understand while developing eight skills: critical thinking, decision-making, problem-solving, resource management, scientific thinking, risk assessment, prioritisation and adaptability.

INFINIX aims to inspire children's interest in space exploration and STEM while encouraging the next generation of scientists, innovators and space explorers.

The project uses HTML for structure, CSS for interface design and JavaScript for interactive gameplay and mission systems. It runs directly in a web browser without requiring installation.

INFINIX transforms real Mars survival challenges into an interactive simulation. Players learn through making decisions, managing resources and handling unexpected emergencies instead of simply reading scientific information.

Our team considered the target audience, scientific accuracy, gameplay difficulty, educational value, user experience and realism. We aimed to create a game that is scientifically meaningful, easy to understand and enjoyable for children aged 7–12.
